gaps.issue: No incoming transition — unreachable within discovery phase. Represents a server-side binding lifecycle pre-condition. Searched section 5.8; no explicit entry transition defined.

Non-terminal state with no outgoing transition. After breaking change introduces new binding URI, no further discovery-phase state is modeled. Searched section 5.8; spec describes URI change but no subsequent discovery re-entry.

Signature verification (sections 8.4.3, 14.3) is a normative client behavior within this state but is not modeled as a distinct sub-state or transition guard. Multiple behavioral constraints (N-8-4-013, N-8-4-014, N-8-4-017, N-14-3-006) describe verification steps with no FSM representation.

No outgoing transitions within initiation phase. TASK_STATE_WORKING is reached via three paths (send_message_requested, send_message_request_received, POST /message:stream) but has no transitions within this stage. Exits to task_execution as inter-stage connection. Searched sections 3.1 and 6.x — confirmed processing continues in task_execution phase.

Only outgoing transition is to STREAM_CLOSED for message-only streams (stream.mode = MESSAGE_ONLY). No outgoing transition modeled for task lifecycle streams where the stream begins with a Task object and continues with status/artifact events. Spec section 3.1.2 confirms task lifecycle streams follow a different closure pattern (close on terminal task state), which belongs to the task_execution phase.

Missing state coverage for direct Message response (non-streaming, no task created). Spec section 3.1.1 states 'Clients send a message to an agent and receive either a task... or a direct response message.' The message-only non-streaming response path has no FSM state to represent the terminal outcome where agent returns a Message without creating a Task. D-3-1-044 post_cond acknowledges this alternative (message.returned = true) but the to_state only models the task creation path.

No transition from TASK_STATE_SUBMITTED to TASK_STATE_WORKING within initiation phase. The task lifecycle diagram shows submitted → working: Start processing as a standard transition. This transition is expected in the task_execution phase, but its absence creates an apparent dead-end for TASK_STATE_SUBMITTED within initiation (only outgoing is to TASK_STATE_REJECTED). TASK_STATE_SUBMITTED effectively serves as a boundary state between initiation and task_execution.

No incoming transition — unreachable. Client initiates subscription from any non-terminal task state but no explicit transition into this state from task states. Searched sections 3.1.6 and 9.4.6; subscription is a client-initiated action orthogonal to task state.

No incoming transition — unreachable. Entered when push notification HTTP delivery fails, but no explicit transition from a prior delivery state exists in the input data. Searched sections 4.3 and 13.2.

No incoming transition — unreachable. Entered when client's webhook receives a push notification from the server, but no explicit transition from a prior state exists in the input data. Searched sections 4.3 and 13.2.

No incoming transition within the interruption phase — unreachable. Streams are opened during task_execution or initiation phases (e.g., via message/stream or tasks/resubscribe). Searched section 11.7; stream creation is defined in streaming setup, not within the interruption lifecycle. STREAM_STATE_OPEN serves as a cross-cutting infrastructure state.

no incoming transition — abstract meta-state representing union of concrete terminal states (COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELED). Entered implicitly when any concrete terminal state is reached. Searched spec section 3.3.2; no explicit transition to this meta-state found.

All candidate exit states in task_execution are semantic_type terminal or have outgoing intra-stage transitions. Terminal states (TASK_STATE_COMPLETED, TASK_STATE_FAILED, TASK_STATE_CANCELED, TASK_STATE_REJECTED, STREAM_CLOSED) satisfy the no-outgoing-transitions criterion but violate the non-terminal exit state heuristic. Terminal-to-terminal crossings were defined as best-available resolution.

Termination stage contains TASK_STATE_WORKING as a non-terminal entry state (listed in entry_from_previous) with transitions to COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELED, REJECTED. These duplicate transitions already present in task_execution. task_execution.TASK_STATE_WORKING has outgoing intra-stage transitions, preventing it from serving as a strict exit candidate. No clean inter-stage connection resolved.

Termination stage contains STREAM_ACTIVE as a non-terminal entry state (listed in entry_from_previous) with transition to STREAM_CLOSED. Could map from task_execution.STREAM_ACTIVE but that state has outgoing intra-stage transitions (self-loop and to STREAM_CLOSED). Overlapping modeling prevents clean boundary resolution.

Termination stage contains STREAM_STATE_OPEN as a non-terminal entry state (listed in entry_from_previous) with transition to STREAM_STATE_CLOSED. Could map from task_execution.STREAM_STATE_OPEN but that state has outgoing intra-stage transitions. Additionally, initiation and interruption stages also contain STREAM_STATE_OPEN, creating a three-way ambiguity.

Initiation stage has terminal states (TASK_STATE_REJECTED, STREAM_CLOSED) representing termination outcomes for tasks rejected or message-only streams closed before reaching task_execution. No boundary is defined between initiation and termination in the stage order, so these terminal states have no inter-stage path to the termination phase.

Authentication stage models TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED as an entry_from_previous with exit via REQUEST_AUTHORIZED back to task_execution for secondary credential flows. However, spec section 7.6 states secondary credentials are obtained out-of-band and provided via subsequent message/send, which flows through the interruption stage (AUTH_REQUIRED → WORKING). No listed boundary supports a task_execution → authentication crossing; the secondary auth loop appears to be modeled redundantly across authentication and interruption stages.

Termination stage contains non-terminal state 'submitted' (lowercase, source D-6-6-012) listed in entry_from_previous, but task_execution and initiation use 'TASK_STATE_SUBMITTED' (uppercase). Naming inconsistency prevents confident pairing. No state named 'submitted' exists in task_execution or initiation.

Termination stage contains non-terminal state 'STREAM_OPEN' (source D-3-1-038) listed in entry_from_previous with transition to STREAM_CLOSED. Task_execution uses 'STREAM_STATE_OPEN' (different name). No state named 'STREAM_OPEN' exists in task_execution. Name mismatch prevents resolution.

Interruption stage contains STREAM_STATE_OPEN with no incoming transitions (flagged as unreachable in B1). Stream may carry over from task_execution when task enters interrupted state, but task_execution already models stream closure on interrupted states via STREAM_ACTIVE → STREAM_CLOSED (guard includes INPUT_REQUIRED, AUTH_REQUIRED). Ambiguous whether a separate inter-stage stream carry-over is required or is redundant with intra-stage stream closure.
